card.title: I Predicted This
card.instruction: Create opportunities to show that each impossible event confirms a theory you understood long before anyone asked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dog's floating. My old notebook predicted household things would rise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says bread. Help me get him down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bread was the first case. My theory always included pets. Try 'sit.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He sat on the ceiling. Now the cat's joining him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Independent confirmation! Bring the notebook; you'll want the chapter on getting them down.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims an old elevation theory, A3 includes pets and applies a sit instruction, and A5 celebrates the second floating animal as independent confirmation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's bread correction and rescue request cause A3's theory extension and command; B4's ceiling sit plus cat causes A5's confirmation and notebook request.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the dog down and B4 reports the actual outcome and new animal development.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's second animal to claim the theory's breadth and direct attention to its supposed practical chapter.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a floating dog and old notebook; B2 gives the immediate rescue task.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's independent-confirmation line is earned by B4's cat rather than a repeated assertion about bread.
